project.title: ExperienceEvo: Artifact-State Transition Experience Learning for Multi-Tool Geospatial Agents
project.target_venue: 中期答辩 / workshop paper / technical report

scope: do not claim eval infrastructure as contribution
do not overclaim Qwen 3B GRPO pending eval

contract.gap: Existing tool-using agents largely plan from language context or retrieve whole textual cases, but they do not explicitly model intermediate artifacts, tool preconditions, parameter binding, output contracts, and evidence-supported continuation in long-horizon geospatial tool chains.
contract.task: Propose and evaluate a non-parametric experience learning method that abstracts historical tool rollouts into executable artifact-state transitions and injects them as state-constrained planning priors.

questions.text: Does artifact-state transition experience improve tool-chain completion and tool planning quality?
Does reliability-aware experience retrieval reduce tool errors and redundant calls?
Can the gains be separated from generic prompting or engineering guards?
Can non-parametric experience reuse complement later parameterized GRPO training?

contract.contribution: Artifact-state transition representation, Q/N/R reliability modeling with Quse, state-constrained step-wise retrieval and injection, and evidence-grounded experience control for multi-tool agents.
nonclaims: Do not claim generic OEA evaluation infrastructure as a method contribution.
Do not claim ordinary answer accuracy improves comprehensively; main gain is tool-chain and generated-artifact-inclusive behavior.
Do not claim current Qwen 3B GRPO evaluation as completed until clean full eval finishes.
Do not claim v4_clean uses embedding retrieval; current main retrieval is deterministic BM25 + structured state ranking + Q/N/R reranking.
